summary: Misrouted prefetch traffic causing reserved-slice starvation in us-west reserved capacity
description:
Issue summary:
Parcelly reported persistent elevated p99 latency and reduced throughput on their dedicated reserved slice in us-west between 2026-03-10T08:00 and ongoing. Symptoms look like capacity starvation on their reserved GPU slice despite available cluster level free slots.

Impact:
- Parcelly experienced 30-60% drop in observed requests/s for batched generation routes.
- Elevated p50/p95/p99 across multi-sequence jobs; customer reported user-facing timeouts on batching-heavy endpoints.
- Affects single reserved slice (customer-dedicated) but other tenants unaffected at cluster level.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (us-west-2) reserved slice: slice-id rs-8473
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Models: redwood-gpt-open-7b (primary), fallback opt-6.7b-q8 for low-cost routes

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) Parcelly reproduces with heavy burst of short streaming requests (median len 60 tokens) and periodic long validation jobs (2k tokens) around 08:00 UTC.
2) Platform autoscaler shows no immediate scale-up (slice remains at target node count).
3) Allocator logs show slots being held by long-running prefetch leases from another tenant cohort routed into same reservation due to a routing mapping change earlier in the day.
4) Requests queue on the reservation; scheduler attempts gang allocation but fails to pack incoming short streams efficiently; p99 rises.

Observed behavior:
- Slot utilization reported as ~95% but effective available GPU memory for Parcelly's tasks drops to ~30% because several slots are occupied by long-prefetch KV caches and lingering connection contexts from unrelated tenant A (noisy cohort).
- Metrics show a spike in prefetch lease acquisitions tied to routing key hash region 'mosaic-12' starting 08:02.
- Autoscaler telemetry indicates low signal (no new nodes provisioned) because cluster-level free slots exist but they are outside the reserved slice boundary.

Expected behavior:
- Reserved slice should honor tenant isolation: prefetch/long-lived background contexts from other tenants must not route into Parcelly's reserved slice. Autoscaler should detect local starvation and trigger refill policies or temporary cross-slice fallback when isolation is violated.

Logs / Dashboards / Links:
- Allocator trace: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/alloc-traces?var=slice=rs-8473&from=2026-03-10T07:50:00&to=2026-03-10T09:10:00
- Autoscaler dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/autoscaler/provisioning?from=2026-03-10T07:00:00&to=2026-03-10T12:00:00
- Customer provided sample request IDs: [req-00ab12, req-00ab34, req-00ab67]
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Support (Anika Shah): Initial triage with Parcelly; confirmed throughput degradation and collected sample request IDs and stack traces. Opened ticket and escalated to infra on-call.

2026-03-10 09:30 - Oncall SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed prefetch lease growth in rs-8473; noted unexpected routing entries that map 'mosaic-12' cohort into the reserved slice. Adding allocator and routing teams.

2026-03-10 10:15 - Allocator Eng (Priya Patel): Found batch of long-lived prefetch contexts from tenant A (ID: ta-991) that were misrouted due to a stale shard map entry after a recent rollout. We'll roll back the shard map and patch routing validation.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Support (Anika Shah): Notified Parcelly of mitigation plan and requested permission for brief controlled rollback window. Customer approved; assigned maint window 11:30-11:40 UTC.

2026-03-10 12:05 - Allocator Eng (Priya Patel): Completed rollback of shard map; removed misrouted lease holders; observed immediate slot reclamation for rs-8473. Parcelly reports partial recovery in throughput.

2026-03-11 08:22 - SRE (Miguel Ortega): Added an interim guard in allocator to reject prefetch leases that originate outside slice owner namespaces. Preparing permanent fix and a regression test for routing map rollouts.
2026-03-12 14:10 - Support (Anika Shah): Parcelly confirmed stabilization over 24h, slight p99 variance during validation jobs but within SLA. Moving to in-progress for follow-up work and postmortem.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Stale shard map after an internal routing rollout allowed cohort 'mosaic-12' prefetch traffic to be mistakenly considered local to rs-8473. Evidence: allocator traces show lease grants with origin tenant 'ta-991' but target slice rs-8473.

Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler did not trigger cross-slice refill because it only considers cluster-unreserved capacity, not per-slice lease fragmentation. Need a metric to surface per-slice effective free-memory rather than slot count.

Partial finding: The allocator grants leases based on soft affinity when slot packing heuristics consider locality; a missing ownership check in the prefetch path was introduced in allocator v2.8.1 (commit 9f2b3ea).
Impact quantification: Observed 45% reduction in Parcelly's batched RPS during the peak 08:02-08:40 window. Other tenants on cluster saw no degradation.
resolution:
Mitigation performed: rolled back the shard map rollout that introduced incorrect routing. Immediate reclamation of misrouted prefetch leases freed effective capacity for the reserved slice and throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.

Follow-up / Next steps:
- Deploy a patch to allocator (PR github.com/redwood-infra/allocator/pull/3982) adding strict owner checks for lease grants and a unit/regression test for shard map rollbacks. (Owner: Priya Patel)
- Add a per-slice free-memory metric and alert when effective free capacity < 20% despite slot count > 0 so autoscaler can trigger emergency refill or fallback policies. (Owner: Miguel Ortega)
- Run a postmortem and include the issue in the Reserved Slice Runbook with steps: detection query, immediate rollback procedure, and customer communication template.
- Customer follow-up: scheduled a post-incident review with Parcelly on 2026-03-15 to review root cause and compensating controls.

Status: Mitigation complete, patch in review, monitoring/alerts planned.
